---
title: "Layout"
---

Ribasim does not use the location of nodes and the geometry of links in the simulation.
But a model that follows the real water system is much easier to review, on the map and in the [model viewer](../viewer.qmd), so the regional models and the coupled model get a shared layout step.
None of this changes the results.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![The input model, with straight links.](https://s3.deltares.nl/ribasim-nl/doc-image/figures/level-3-input-model.png){fig-alt="Coloured Basin areas with straight links."}

![The final model, with links along the watercourses, and Junctions where they join.](https://s3.deltares.nl/ribasim-nl/doc-image/figures/level-4-forcing.png){fig-alt="The same area, with links that follow the watercourses."}
:::

## Routing the links

The input model of a level controlled water authority has a connector node where a hydro-object crosses the boundary of a peilgebied, see [Level controlled](level-controlled.qmd).
The structure itself is often some distance along the hydro-object, so at the end of the forcing stage `ribasim_nl.structure_locations.move_to_structures` first moves these nodes to their structure:

- A Pump moves to the gemaal that its crossing is matched with, if that is within 100 m.
- An Outlet moves to the stuw that its crossing is matched with. An Outlet without one stands for all crossings between its two areas that have no structure of their own. It moves to a stuw within 250 m that lies on a hydro-object of one of these crossings, or on a hydro-object that touches it, such as the weir behind an inlet culvert.
- A structure gets one node, the nearest one.

A node with a structure gets its code in `meta_code_waterbeheerder`.
The koppeltabel of the measured discharges refers to nodes by their key, see [Node keys](../dev/node-keys.qmd), so a moved node is found where it is.
This is not done when the input model is made, since the parametrization depends on where nodes are, such as within supply areas, and a node whose type a feedback form changes gets its key from its location.

Then `ribasim_nl.network_snapping.snap_model` aligns the layout with the hydro-objects in `verwerkt/profielen/network.gpkg`, which are written by the [profile generation](profile-generation.qmd):

- Links between a Basin and a connector node follow the hydro-objects. The Top10NL water lines fill the gaps between them: they cost 3 times as much per metre, since the Top10NL has every ditch, and the shortest route would leave the hydro-objects wherever a ditch cuts a corner. Hydro-objects are only connected where there is evidence: the culverts (`duikersifonhevel`) of the crossings data, gaps of at most 2 m, and gaps across BGT water surfaces. A culvert with both ends in the basin area is used whole, such as a siphon under a canal of another Basin ([#1078](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/1078)). Connector nodes far from the hydro-objects are connected over the BGT water surfaces, crossing at most 100 m of land.
- A connector node that is not reached within the basin area lies beyond a gap in it, such as a canal of another authority that splits the area, or outside it, where the model connects it over a distance. The links of its Basin are then routed again, also along the lines and the water in a strip around the straight line from the node to the routes found, see `ribasim_nl.network_snapping.reach_area`. The strip reaches 250 m to both sides, or a quarter of its length, up to 1000 m. Beyond the basin area a line costs twice as much per metre, so routes stay within the area where they can ([#1079](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/pull/1079)).
- Basin nodes are moved to the centre of this network within their basin area: the point from which the routes to their connector nodes are cheapest in total. The point of the network nearest to where the Basin node was counts as one more node to reach, so a Basin with a single connector node stays there.
- Links stay straight if no such route is found, or if it is not less than `ribasim_nl.link_geometries.MAX_STRAIGHT_LINE_RATIO` times longer than the straight line, the same threshold as for the gravity controlled models. A Basin node also stays where it is if fewer than half of its links can be routed from the centre.

In the gravity controlled models, `snap_to_waterways` routes the links that are still straight along the Top10NL waterways, at the end of their dynamic stage.
The routes that the other links of their Basin follow already are part of that network, and cost a third of the Top10NL lines per metre, so the pumps of one gemaal share their route instead of each following another ditch.
Such a route gets a point where a link leaves it, so the two are merged up to there.

The link of an RWZI follows the waterway from its discharge point to the route of its Basin in the same way, and joins the route where that waterway meets it, see `ribasim_nl.rwzi.attach_rwzi_junctions`.
Without a waterway it goes straight to the nearest point of the route.

## Tidying

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  a["Route links"] --> b["junctionify<br>merge shared parts<br>of links"]
  b --> c["tidy_layout"]
```

`ribasim_nl.junctionify` merges the shared parts of links into Junctions, and `ribasim_nl.layout.tidy_layout` makes sure no nodes are on top of each other and no links overlap.

The inflows and outflows of a Basin share one Junction tree, so each waterway is drawn once, see `ribasim_nl.flow_paths.merge_basin_trees`.
The trees are merged after the last nodes are added to a model, so only the IDs of Junctions change.
An RWZI Junction that discharges on a route stays where it is, and the other routes along the link it split join there, so they do not run side by side beyond it ([#1065](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/1065)).
Ribasim connects a group of Junctions with one Basin as a neighbour with that Basin, in the direction of the link of each other neighbour with the group, see [Junction](https://ribasim.org/reference/node/junction.html).
The direction of the links within the tree, and with the Basin, does not change the simulation, only the sign of their flow, see `ribasim_nl.flow_paths.towards_basin`.
A link that only carries inflows points towards the Basin, and one that only carries outflows away from it.
A link that carries both follows the main flow: the direction in which the waterway lines it follows are digitized, where they cover most of it, such as the network of Rijkswaterstaat.
Elsewhere it points to the side that can drain the most, in the `afvoer` control state, where ManningResistances and placeholder capacities are unlimited.
`ribasim_nl.flow_paths.Routes` follows the links through Junctions in the same way as Ribasim.

A measured series that adds the flows of several nodes is observed on a Junction that combines exactly those nodes, see `ribasim_nl.observations`.
Where the merged tree has no such Junction, for instance because the links of a gemaal and the inlet next to it meet at the Basin node, `ribasim_nl.flow_paths.combine_nodes` makes one on the link of the first node, if the nodes are within 250 m of it.

- Bergend Basins are placed 100 m from their doorgaand Basin.
- Junctions within 25 m of the BGT water, but not on it, move onto the water.
- Nodes that are still within 10 m of each other are moved apart, Junctions to a free place on the water if there is one.
- Links that still overlap, such as those of neighbouring Basins along a shared waterway, are offset 5 m.

The gravity controlled models get the same layout step at the end of their dynamic stage, and `ribasim_nl.validation.validate_model` checks it.
It also checks that the Basin areas are valid and have no slivers: parts and holes that are on average at most 1 mm wide, which draw as lines on the map.
`Model.clean_basin_area` fixes both in the regional models and the Rijkswaterstaat model.
The [coupling](couple.qmd) tidies the links between models in the same way, and first rebuilds the routes of the Basins of Rijkswaterstaat, as the Rijkswaterstaat model does, see `ribasim_nl.flow_paths.rebuild_rws_junction_trees`.
These follow the network of Rijkswaterstaat, and the Top10NL water lines at 3 times the cost per metre. Nodes far from these lines are routed over the Top10NL water surfaces, and nodes beyond the area of the Basin in the strip around the straight line to them, as in the regional models. Only the nodes that are still not reached branch off straight from the nearest point of the routes.
A link between two regional models follows the routes of the links of its Basin, and the Top10NL from where it leaves them, like a link that is routed later in a gravity controlled model.
A link that is still straight, with its node within 100 m of the routes of its Basin, follows them up to the nearest point and goes straight from there, see `ribasim_nl.flow_paths.branch_off_routes`.
In open water the network of Rijkswaterstaat only has a few straight lines, so there the routes follow the fairways of OpenStreetMap ([#1010](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/1010)). Open water is a Basin that is on average more than 750 m wide, twice its area over its perimeter, such as the IJsselmeer, the Markermeer, the Oosterschelde and the Haringvliet.
Nodes on the shore branch off straight from the nearest point of a fairway from which the line crosses at most 100 m of land, and nodes close together share such a line.
The hydro-objects of the water authorities on the water of a lake, such as the channel of a harbour, are part of its network, joined to the fairways along the cheapest path over water, so the nodes in a harbour follow its channel ([#1078](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/1078)).
The Junctions that the coupling adds move onto the BGT water, as in the regional models.
